title: FTP server accepts anonymous login
evidence: 172.17.0.3:21 returned 230 for USER anonymous; anyone can list and download from the public area
remediation:
Disable anonymous FTP unless the directory served is genuinely
intended for public download (which is almost never the modern
pattern). vsftpd: anonymous_enable=NO. proftpd: AnonymousAuthAllowed
off. ftpd-BSD: -A flag. Where public download IS required, move
to HTTPS so credentials and listings are not negotiable in
cleartext.

title: FTP server accepts default credentials
evidence: 172.17.0.3:21 authenticated as anonymous:anonymous@example.com
remediation:
Disable anonymous FTP if not strictly required. Change default
credentials, enforce a strong password policy, and migrate to SFTP or
FTPS so credentials are not exposed on the wire.

title: FTP server does not offer AUTH TLS
evidence: 172.17.0.3:21 FEAT response omits AUTH TLS/SSL; control and data channels are forced to cleartext
remediation:
Migrate the listener to FTPS (FTP-over-TLS via AUTH TLS) or
replace FTP with SFTP entirely. vsftpd: ssl_enable=YES,
force_local_data_ssl=YES, force_local_logins_ssl=YES. Cleartext
FTP transmits the password and every file in plaintext, with
zero protection against MITM credential capture or content
modification.

title: vsftpd 2.3.4 backdoor (CVE-2011-2523)
evidence: 172.17.0.3:21 banner identifies vsftpd 2.3.4, which shipped with a backdoor root shell on port 6200 triggered by a USER ending with ":)"
remediation:
Replace the vsftpd 2.3.4 binary immediately. The official source
tarball was tampered with on the mirror in July 2011 and contains
a hard-coded shell on port 6200. Any sender of "USER xyz:)\\r\\n"
pops an unauthenticated root shell. Upgrade to a current vsftpd
release shipped by your distribution and verify the binary
checksum against the upstream signing key.

title: OpenSSH end-of-life version
evidence: 172.17.0.3:22 runs an EOL OpenSSH release: SSH-2.0-OpenSSH_4.7p1 Debian-8ubuntu1
remediation:
Upgrade OpenSSH to the current stable release (>= 9.0). Older OpenSSH
versions ship vulnerable defaults (CBC ciphers, ssh-dss host keys,
hmac-sha1) and several enumerable CVEs accumulate per minor version.
On Debian/Ubuntu: apt full-upgrade openssh-server.

title: SSH server permits CBC-mode ciphers (CVE-2008-5161)
evidence: 172.17.0.3:22 accepts CBC-mode ciphers in S2C/C2S algorithm lists
remediation:
Remove CBC ciphers from /etc/ssh/sshd_config "Ciphers" line. Keep only
AEAD constructions (chacha20-poly1305@openssh.com, aes128-gcm@openssh.com,
aes256-gcm@openssh.com) and CTR fallbacks (aes128-ctr, aes192-ctr,
aes256-ctr). Reload sshd.

title: SSH server accepts default credentials
evidence: 172.17.0.3:22 authenticated as user:user
remediation:
Change default credentials immediately. Disable password
authentication where possible (PasswordAuthentication no in sshd_config)
and enforce key-based authentication. Where passwords are unavoidable,
enforce a strong password policy and rotate compromised passwords.

title: SSH key exchange offers diffie-hellman-group1-sha1 (1024-bit MODP)
evidence: 172.17.0.3:22 kex_algorithms contains diffie-hellman-group1-sha1 (1024-bit MODP, LOGJAM-class weakness)
remediation:
Remove diffie-hellman-group1-sha1 from /etc/ssh/sshd_config "KexAlgorithms"
line. Prefer curve25519-sha256 and DH groups >= 3072 bits
(diffie-hellman-group16-sha512, diffie-hellman-group18-sha512).

title: SSH server offers deprecated DSA (ssh-dss) host key
evidence: 172.17.0.3:22 advertises ssh-dss host key (banner: SSH-2.0-OpenSSH_4.7p1 Debian-8ubuntu1)
remediation:
DSA host keys were disabled by default in OpenSSH 7.0 (2015) due to
forensic recoverability of the per-message nonce. Regenerate the
server host key set without DSA:
  rm /etc/ssh/ssh_host_dsa_key*
  ssh-keygen -A
and ensure /etc/ssh/sshd_config does not enumerate HostKey ssh_host_dsa_key.

title: SSH server permits weak MAC algorithms (MD5 / SHA-1)
evidence: 172.17.0.3:22 permits MD5/SHA-1 MAC algorithms
remediation:
Restrict MACs to SHA-2 / Encrypt-then-MAC constructions only. In
/etc/ssh/sshd_config add:
  MACs hmac-sha2-256-etm@openssh.com,hmac-sha2-512-etm@openssh.com,umac-128-etm@openssh.com
Reload sshd.

title: Telnet service exposed (cleartext protocol)
evidence: 172.17.0.3:23 is running a Telnet listener; usernames, passwords, and session data cross the wire in plaintext
remediation:
Replace Telnet with SSH. Every modern OS ships an OpenSSH-compatible
server. Disable telnetd (systemctl disable inetd / disable telnet
service on network appliances). If the host is a legacy industrial
device that cannot do SSH, terminate Telnet inside a VPN or jump
host and never expose port 23 on the routed network.

title: Telnet server does not offer the ENCRYPT option
evidence: 172.17.0.3:23 IAC negotiation does not advertise the ENCRYPT (38) option; the session is unencrypted
remediation:
RFC 2946 telnet-with-encryption is rare in the field; rather than
trying to enable it on the device, decommission Telnet altogether
and run SSH. Keeping a Telnet listener even with line-mode
encryption negotiated leaves the option for any client to opt out
and revert to cleartext.

title: SMTP banner discloses MTA product and version
evidence: 172.17.0.3:25 220 banner advertises MTA product/version: 220 metasploitable.localdomain ESMTP Postfix (Ubuntu)
remediation:
Strip the MTA name and version from the 220 greeting. Postfix:
smtpd_banner = $myhostname ESMTP. Sendmail: define(`confSMTP_LOGIN_MSG\\').
Exim: smtp_banner = $primary_hostname ESMTP. Version disclosure
helps an attacker pick a CVE-specific exploit (CVE-2019-10149
Exim, CVE-2017-7693 Postfix, etc.) without further probing.

title: NFS server registered with portmap
evidence: 172.17.0.3:111 portmap lists NFS (program 100003); mountd port = 50419
remediation:
An NFS listener visible from outside the host network is a frequent
source of accidental file-sharing exposures. Confirm the service is
intentional. If it is, restrict TCP/UDP 2049 plus the mountd
ephemeral port (or pin mountd via /etc/nfs.conf "port = 32767") to
the storage VLAN, require Kerberos sec=krb5p, and disable
rpcbind/portmap on hosts that don't need RPC discovery.

title: SunRPC portmapper exposes program listing
evidence: 172.17.0.3:111 portmap DUMP returned 21 programs: portmapper/v2/tcp:111 nfs/v2/udp:2049 nfs/v3/udp:2049 nfs/v4/udp:2049 nlockmgr/v1/udp:58022 nlockmgr/v3/udp:58022 nlockmgr/v4/udp:58022 nfs/v2/tcp:2049 nfs/v3/tcp:2049 nfs/v4/tcp:2049 nlockmgr/v1/tcp:33414 nlockmgr/v3/tcp:33414 nlockmgr/v4/tcp:33414 mountd/v1/udp:58275 mountd/v1/tcp:50419 mountd/v2/udp:58275 mountd/v2/tcp:50419 mountd/v3/udp:58275 mountd/v3/tcp:50419 status/v1/udp:49024 status/v1/tcp:42939
remediation:
rpcbind / portmap is the discovery oracle for every SunRPC service on
the host (NFS, NIS, NLM, etc.). If the box does not need to publish
RPC services to the network, stop rpcbind. Otherwise, restrict TCP/111
and UDP/111 to the management subnet via host firewall, and run
rpcbind with -w -h <bind-iface> to scope the listener.

title: SMB signing not required (NTLM relay target)
evidence: 172.17.0.3:139 does not require SMB signing (server accepts unsigned packets)
remediation:
Enforce SMB signing on the server. Windows domain controllers:
enabled by default; member servers and workstations: Group Policy
"Microsoft network server: Digitally sign communications (always)" = Enabled.
Samba: in smb.conf set "server signing = mandatory", restart smbd.
Without signing, the host is a valid target for NTLM relay attacks
(mitm6 + ntlmrelayx).

title: SMB v1 protocol supported
evidence: 172.17.0.3:139 accepts SMB1 NEGOTIATE PROTOCOL (CIFS dialect)
remediation:
Disable SMBv1 entirely. Windows: remove the "SMB 1.0/CIFS File Sharing
Support" feature, or via PowerShell:
  Set-SmbServerConfiguration -EnableSMB1Protocol $false
Samba: in smb.conf set "min protocol = SMB2", restart smbd.
SMBv1 carries CVE-2017-0144 (EternalBlue) and the broader ETERNAL*
exploit family.

title: MySQL server accepts default credentials
evidence: 172.17.0.3:3306 authenticated as root:
remediation:
Change the root password immediately. Run mysql_secure_installation,
remove anonymous users, restrict root login to localhost, and create
least-privilege application accounts in place of root.

title: MySQL end-of-life version
evidence: 172.17.0.3:3306 runs an EOL MySQL release: 5.0.51a-3ubuntu5
remediation:
Upgrade MySQL to a supported branch. MySQL 5.6 reached EOL in
February 2021, 5.5 in December 2018, and earlier branches years
before that. Migrate to MySQL 8.0 (or MariaDB 10.6 / 10.11 LTS)
and apply current patches. EOL releases accumulate unpatched
privilege-escalation and auth-bypass CVEs (CVE-2021-2154,
CVE-2018-2696, CVE-2016-6662 etc).

title: MySQL server version disclosed in handshake
evidence: 172.17.0.3:3306 announces server version 5.0.51a-3ubuntu5 in its initial Handshake V10 packet
remediation:
The server version is part of the MySQL handshake and cannot be
removed without patching the daemon. Network segmentation and
firewalling the database port to application hosts is the practical
mitigation. Version disclosure assists attackers in selecting
CVE-specific exploits.

title: PostgreSQL uses deprecated MD5 password authentication
evidence: 172.17.0.3:5432 responded AuthenticationMD5Password (type=5); MD5 password storage was deprecated by upstream in PG14 (2021)
remediation:
Migrate to SCRAM-SHA-256. In postgresql.conf set
  password_encryption = scram-sha-256
Have each user re-set their password (\\password in psql) so the
hash is re-stored under SCRAM. Then change pg_hba.conf entries
from "md5" to "scram-sha-256". MD5 hashes are unsalted across
users (salt = username) and can be replayed if leaked.

title: VNC server speaks legacy RFB 3.3
evidence: 172.17.0.3:5900 negotiates RFB 003.003; server unilaterally picks the security type, no SecurityResult phase, weak VNC-Auth is the only common option
remediation:
Upgrade the VNC server to a build that speaks RFB 3.7 or 3.8. RFB 3.3
predates the security-type negotiation phase and cannot offer
VeNCrypt / TLS / SASL transports; an MITM cannot be detected by the
client. Modern tightvnc / tigervnc / realvnc default to RFB 3.8.

title: VNC server offers VNCAuth (DES-based, 8-char truncation)
evidence: 172.17.0.3:5900 offers VNCAuth (security type 2); the password is truncated to 8 characters and protected by a 64-bit DES challenge/response, brute-forceable offline once a challenge is captured
remediation:
Disable VNCAuth and require a stronger security type. Configure the
VNC server for VeNCrypt+x509 (TLS-tunneled VNC) or SASL, or front the
service with SSH/TLS at the network layer. Avoid relying on the
8-character VNC password as an access control.

title: OS family inferred from service banners
evidence: 172.17.0.3 OS family Linux (Linux (Ubuntu)) inferred at 80% confidence from signals: [ssh_banner contains Ubuntu ssh_banner contains Debian smtp_banner contains Postfix mysql_version contains debian/ubuntu/linux]
remediation:
This is an informational fingerprint derived from the application
banners we already collected (SSH, SMB, HTTP, FTP). It does not
imply a vulnerability on its own. Where the OS family or release
drives a compliance or EOL finding (Windows 2008, kernel 3.x,
etc.) the matching plugin in plugins/os/ will fire separately.
